summary: One field many agents share: compute once when the goal moves, not once per agent.
overview: Places a grid in the world, auto-detects obstacles by physics overlap so you never hand-author a blocked-cell array, and computes a direction for every cell pointing toward the goal. Recompute when the goal moves — ONCE, not per agent — and every agent using the grid reads its own cell.
That is the whole reason to prefer it over per-agent pathfinding for crowds: a hundred agents cost one field, not a hundred searches.

features.name: Flow field
features.what: the algorithm itself, plain C# so it is testable without a scene.

features.name: Flow field grid
features.what: places the grid in the world and bakes obstacles from physics.

features.name: Flow field agent
features.what: drops on any number of movers; each samples its current cell and follows the arrow.

useCases: A crowd or swarm all heading for the same place.
Tower-defence enemies streaming toward the base.
Any case where per-agent pathfinding is the frame's biggest cost.

walkthrough.name: Width / Height
walkthrough.what: Cells across and deep. Cost is proportional to width times height, which is why the defaults are modest.

walkthrough.name: Cell Size
walkthrough.what: World size of one cell. Larger cells mean a cheaper field and coarser paths.

walkthrough.name: Obstacle Mask
walkthrough.what: Layers checked when baking which cells are blocked.

walkthrough.name: Obstacle Check Radius / Height
walkthrough.what: The box used to test each cell. Too small and thin walls are missed; too large and doorways close up.

walkthrough.name: Recompute Field
walkthrough.what: Call when the goal moves. Once per move, not once per agent.

gotchas.title: It is only worth it for many agents
gotchas.body: For one or two, a normal path search is cheaper and more accurate. The win comes entirely from sharing one field.

gotchas.title: Obstacles are baked, not live
gotchas.body: A door that opens after the bake is still a wall to the field. Re-bake when the layout changes.

gotchas.title: Agents follow cell arrows, so paths look grid-like
gotchas.body: Movement snaps toward cell directions rather than curving smoothly. Smaller cells help; smoothing on the agent helps more.
